corrections: Circle Q2 2026 10-Q's 19.5% daily weighted-average USDC-on-platform metric and $12.442B end balance are Circle's own platform metrics, not Coinbase's. Note 1579 defines Circle's platform as Circle Mint, corporate-held USDC and Circle wallet products.

Coinbase's separate Q3 2026 average USDC held in Coinbase products is $22B, up 49% YoY, per its October 29 earnings release. The Q3 10-Q says the average reached an all-time high but does not quantify it in the cited section.

SBI Holdings and SBI Shinsei Bank each invested $25M in Circle at its 2025 IPO; Circle SBI Japan K.K./SBI Circle Holdings is a 50/50 JV. Circle's Q2 filing says Circle controls/consolidates it as a VIE and it had no significant operating results through June 30, 2026.

SBI has separate historical equity exposure to Ripple (approximately 9% as of June 2025) and 60% voting rights in SBI Ripple Asia as of March 31, 2026. This is an SBI-mediated indirect Circle-Ripple network, not a direct Circle-Ripple partnership.
new_relationships: Circle-Binance: $100M equity investment and five-year USDC promotion agreement; monthly incentive fee tied to USDC held through Circle Modular Smart Contract Wallet infrastructure; SEC 8-K primary evidence.
Coinbase-Circle: Coinbase renewed its Circle arrangement on the same terms in Q3 2026; Circle's Q2 filing reports $324.6M Q2/$655.3M H1 distribution costs under Coinbase agreements.
Coinbase-RLUSD: multi-issuer distribution continues alongside Circle-USDC; token-level balances/revenue splits unknown.
SBI-Circle-Ripple: SBI group has direct capital/operating relationships with both issuers; shared XRPL deployments do not prove a joint Circle-Ripple commercial arrangement.
